title: v1-chat contract normalizer: fncall handshake and framed JSON streaming output
author: Asha Patel
body: Context: Customers using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface reported subtle incompatibilities when mixing legacy chat params (roles, stop arrays, logprobs) with Redwood's framed streaming + function-calling behavior. This PR introduces a contract-normalizer layer that deterministically maps /v1 chat params to Redwood's internal request contract, while preserving streaming semantics and ensuring safe fncall handoffs across fragment boundaries. Motivation: 1) Surface parity for common OpenAI params so customers can switch to Redwood with minimal changes, 2) Reduce stream-desync incidents where function call boundaries are split across fragments, 3) Provide an explicit output shaping contract for structured JSON responses for downstream parsers and SDKs. Summary of changes: - Introduce api/compat/v1_contract_normalizer.go: top-level translator that coalesces roles, stop/stop_sequences, temperature/top_p precedence, and logprobs requests into a single canonical contract. The normalizer documents precedence rules (explicit stop > stop_sequences > model defaults) and normalizes role aliases (assistant/assistant_role -> assistant). - Add runtime/streaming/framed_json_envelope.go: defines the framed JSON envelope used on the wire for streaming tokens/partial-objects, with deterministic sentinel placement for function calls and a fragment-level checksum to detect mid-stream corruption. - Implement fncall/handshake.go: a deterministic handshake protocol used when the model wants to invoke a tool/function. The handshake guarantees that if a function call spans multiple stream fragments, the receiver can reconstruct the call without dropping tokens or duplicating arguments. - Update sdk/typescript/openai_compat_adapter.ts and sdk/python/openai_compat_adapter.py: expose a single compatibility shim that accepts /v1/chat.completions style payloads and forwards them through the new normalizer. Add tests and examples demonstrating role aliasing, multi-stop arrays, and logprob toggles. - Docs: docs/openai_compat/v1_chat_contract.md with the precedence matrix, migration notes, and small examples. - E2E tests: test/compat/test_v1_compat_streaming.py and test/compat/test_fncall_fragment_reassembly.ts to simulate flaky networks and verify correct reassembly/handshake behavior. Checklist: [x] Contract normalizer implementation [x] Handshake protocol with unit tests [x] Streaming framing and checksum [x] SDK adapters updated (TS + Py) [x] Documentation with migration guide [x] E2E tests that simulate fragmentation and replay Motivation details: Most customer breakages came from two real-world patterns: 1) Stop arrays mixed with streaming frames causing early termination tokens to be misinterpreted, and 2) Function call argument objects being split across frames which caused SDKs to attempt JSON reparse on invalid fragments. The normalizer ensures stop semantics are applied deterministically at the earliest safe point; the handshake provides idempotent reassembly. Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c: initial contract-normalizer prototype and tests - 2d3e4f: framing envelope and checksum; wire behavior tests - 4f5g6h: fncall handshake state machine and reassembly tests - 7h8i9j: SDK adapters and examples - 9k0l1m: docs and migration guide - ab2cd3: e2e flaky-network tests Review summary: - Liam O'Connor (review) — "Overall approach looks good. Two ask items: make the fragment checksum optional on legacy clients and add a small perf note about the extra CPU cost of checksuming for high-throughput paths." Response: "Made checksum opt-in via request.contract.checksum=false and added perf note to docs with microbenchmarks showing ~1.8% CPU overhead on p3.8xlarge under our benchmark load." - María González (review) — "Please be explicit in the normalizer doc about stop precedence when stop token overlaps model eos; add a test that reproduces it." Response: "Added test stop_eos_overlap in test_v1_compat_streaming.py and extended the docs with precedence matrix and rationale." - Evan Cho (approval) — "Approach approved; small nits on naming which I left inline." Response: "Addressed naming nits and shortened some exported identifiers to match SDK style guides." CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests (flaky network sim): pass on second rerun (one transient failure on first run due to infra timeout) - linters/formatters: pass - benchmark smoke: pass (baseline latency unchanged within noise) Files changed (high-level): ["api/compat/v1_contract_normalizer.go", "runtime/streaming/framed_json_envelope.go", "runtime/streaming/framed_json_envelope_test.go", "runtime/fncall/handshake.go", "sdk/typescript/openai_compat_adapter.ts", "sdk/python/openai_compat_adapter.py", "docs/openai_compat/v1_chat_contract.md"] Testing and QA notes: - Added deterministic replay harness in test/compat to inject fragment drops/duplicates. - Covered both sync and streaming SDK adapters. - Ran canary on staging for 48h against a traffic slice of customers that previously filed compatibility issues — no regressions observed. Rollout and migration notes: - Default behavior remains backward compatible; checksum/framed envelope is enabled for new clients that opt into the v1 compatibility shim. - We will ship a minor SDK bump (TS/Py) and recommend customers set client.compat_mode = "v1-framed-json" to enable the improved handoff semantics. - Monitor channels: increased sampling of stream-fragment errors and function-call reassembly metrics for first 2 weeks post-merge. Merge: squash merged on 2025-02-20 by María González. Changelog / release notes: - Add deterministic v1 chat contract normalizer to improve OpenAI /v1 chat compatibility and reduce stream fragmentation issues - Introduce framed JSON streaming envelope with optional checksums - Add fncall handshake protocol to guarantee function-call reassembly across fragments - Update TS and Python SDK adapters and add migration docs for clients Impact and follow-ups: - ENG-2310: Add Go SDK adapter follow-up (left as TODO in code) - ENG-2331: Perf tune checksum and add optional hardware-accelerated CRC path - Monitor: new metrics stream.fragment.reassembly.success_rate and api.compat.v1_migration.adoption

release_notes: Deterministic v1 chat contract normalizer, framed JSON streaming envelope with optional checksum, and fncall handshake for robust function-call reassembly across streamed fragments. SDK updates (TS/Py) and migration guide added.
notes_for_support: If customers observe missing fncall args when using older SDKs, advise toggling client.compat_mode to default (legacy) or upgrade SDK to v1-framed-json. Use stream.fragment.reassembly.success_rate metric to validate fix.
